parts.problem_md:
In a cycling club, the number of members are in the ratio males : females = 8 : 3. The club has 342 females.

i) Find the total number of members.

[2]

ii) Find the percentage of the total number of members that are female.

................................................ % [1]
parts.solution_md:
> *i) Write down the fraction of the club members that are female.*

$\frac{3}{8+3}=\frac{3}{11}$

> *Divide the total number of females by the fraction of the club members that are female to work out the total number of club members.*

$342\div\frac{3}{11}$

**[1]**

**1254 ****[1]**

> *ii) Divide the number of female members by the total number of members and multiply by 100% to work out percentage of members that are female.*

$\frac{342}{1254}\times100=27.27272...$

**27.3%**** [1]**

**Answers of 27.27... will also be accepted.**

equations.alt: fraction numerator 3 over denominator 8 plus 3 end fraction equals 3 over 11
342 divided by 3 over 11
342 over 1254 cross times 100 equals 27.27272...

parts.problem_md:
Arjun and Gretal each pay rent.

In 2018, the ratio of the amount each paid in rent was Arjun : Gretal = 5 : 7. 
In 2019, the ratio of the amount each paid in rent was Arjun : Gretal = 9 : 13.

Arjun paid the same amount of rent in both 2018 and 2019. 
Gretal paid \$290 more rent in 2019 than she did in 2018.

Work out the amount Arjun paid in rent in 2019.

\$ ................................................
parts.solution_md:
> *First convert the ratios for each year and person to fractions out of the total rent.*

*In 2018, Arjun pays *$\frac{5}{5+7}=\frac{5}{12}$* of the total rent.  In 2019, Arjun pays *$\frac{9}{9+13}=\frac{9}{22}$* of the total rent.*

* In 2018, Greta pays *$\frac{7}{5+7}=\frac{7}{12}$* of the total rent.  In 2019, Greta pays *$\frac{13}{9+13}=\frac{13}{22}$* of the total rent.*

> *Letting **T*<sub>*1*</sub>* be the total rent paid in 2018 and **T*<sub>*2*</sub>* the total rent paid in 2019, we can write two equations in **T*<sub>*1*</sub>* and **T*<sub>*2*</sub>* using the given information. Arjun pays the same in 2018 and 2019:*

$\frac{9}{22}T_{2}=\frac{5}{12}T_{1}$

> *Greta pays \$290 more in 2019 than 2018:*

$\frac{13}{22}T_{2}=\frac{7}{12}T_{1}+290$

**[1]**

> *The question asks for Arjun's rent in 2019 so we only need to find **T*<sub>*2. *</sub>*Solve the two equations simultaneously, eliminating **T*<sub>*1*</sub>*. Rearrange the first equation to find **T*<sub>*1*</sub>* in terms of **T*<sub>*2*</sub>*.*

$T_{1}=\frac{9\times12}{22\times5}T_{2}=\frac{108}{110}T_{2}=\frac{54}{55}T_{2}$

> *Now substitute **T*<sub>*1*</sub>* into the second equation.*

`therefore 13 over 22 T subscript 2 equals 7 over 12 open parentheses 54 over 55 T subscript 2 close parentheses plus 290`

**[1]**

> *Rearrange and solve for **T*<sub>*2*</sub>*.*

`table row cell 13 over 22 T subscript 2 minus 63 over 110 T subscript 2 end cell equals 290 row cell 1 over 55 T subscript 2 end cell equals 290 row cell T subscript 2 end cell equals cell 15 space 950 end cell end table`

**[1]**

> *In 2019, Arjun pays *$\frac{9}{22}$* of the total rent, so find the amount he pays by multiply this fraction by the total rent for 2019 (**T*<sub>*2*</sub>*).*

$\frac{9}{22}\times15950=6525$

**\$6525*** ***[1]**

**Whole number of US Dollars so two decimal places are not required.**

parts.problem_md:
For a morning flight, the costs of tickets are in the ratio

First Class : Premium : Economy = 14 : 6 : 5.

The cost of a Premium ticket is \$114.

Calculate the cost of a First Class ticket and the cost of an Economy ticket.

First Class \$ ................................................

Economy \$ .................................................
parts.solution_md:
> *Find the multiplier by dividing the cost of a premium ticket by the ratio for a premium ticket. *

*114 ÷ 6 = 19*

**[1]**

> *Multiply the other two parts by this multiplier.*

*14 × 19 = 266 5 × 19 = 95*

**First Class = \$266**** ****[1] **

parts.problem_md:
Amol and Priya deliver 645 parcels in the ratio Amol : Priya = 11 : 4.
Calculate the number of parcels Amol delivers.
parts.solution_md:
> *Find the total of the parts of the ratio.*

*11 + 4 = 15 parts in total*

> *Find the number of parcels that corresponds to one part in the ratio. Divide the total number of parcels by the total number of parts.*

*645 ÷ 15 = 43 parcels per part*

**[1]**

> *Find the number of parcels delivered by Amol by multiplying his number of parts by 43.*

*43 × 11*

**Amol delivers 473 parcels** **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
Here is a list of ingredients to make 20 biscuits.

![cie-igcse-2018-may-jun-2-p4-q1a](assets/001-cie-igcse-2018-may-jun-2-p4-q1a.png)

i) Find the mass of butter needed to make 35 of these biscuits.

............................................. g [2]

ii) Michel has 2 kg of each ingredient.

Work out the greatest number of these biscuits that he can make.

[3]
parts.solution_md:
i) *Method 1  *

> *260 g of butter makes 20 biscuits, so divide 260 g by 20 to find the mass needed to make one biscuit.*

*260 ÷ 20 = 13 g*

> *Multiply 13 g by 35 to find the mass for 35 biscuits.*

*13 × 35 = 455*

* ** dividing by 20 and multiplying by 35*** ****[1]**

*Answer = 455 g ***[1]**

> *Method 2  *

> *260 g of butter makes 20 biscuits. To scale up to 35, multiply 260 by *$\frac{35}{20}$

*260 *$\times\frac{35}{20}$* = 455*

**[1]**

**Answer = 455 g**** ****[1]**

ii) *Method 1  *

*The ingredient with the largest mass is the flour. So how many biscuits Michel can make depends on how many biscuits can be made with 2 kg of flour.* *650 g makes 20 biscuits. Find how much flour is need for one biscuit by dividing 650g by 20.*

*650 ÷ 20 = 32.5*

**[1]**

> *2kg is 2000g. Find out how many times 32.5 g will divide into 2000 g.*

*2000 ÷ 32.5 = 61.53846154...*

**[1]**

> *The greatest number of biscuits that can be made is a whole number. If "61.5..." biscuits, there is not enough flour for 62 biscuits, so round down to 61.*

** ****61 biscuits ****[1]**

> *Method 2  *

*The ingredient with the largest mass is the flour. So how many biscuits Michel can make depends on how many biscuits can be made with 2 kg of flour.* *2 kg is 2000 g. And 650 g of flour makes 20 biscuits.*

> * To scale up 650 g to 2000g, we would multiply by *$\frac{2000}{650}$*. We can scale up 20 biscuits by multiplying by the same ratio.*

*20 *$\times\frac{2000}{650}$* = 61.53846154...*

* **multiplying 20 by *$\frac{2000}{650}$**[1]**

* obtaining 61.5... ***[1]**

> *The greatest number of biscuits that can be made is a whole number. If "61.5..." biscuits, there is not enough flour for 62 biscuits, so round down to 61.*

**61 biscuits ****[1]**

equations.alt: 35 over 20
cross times 35 over 20
cross times 2000 over 650

The fares for a train journey are shown in the table below.

| From London to Marseille | Standard fare | Premier fare |
|---|---|---|
| Adult | \$84 | \$140 |
| Child | \$60 | \$96 |

For one journey from London to Marseille, the ratio

number of adults : number of children = 11 : 2.

There were 220 adults in total on this journey. 
All of the children and 70% of the adults paid the standard fare.  The remaining adults paid the premier fare.
Calculate the total of the fares paid by the adults and the children.

parts.solution_md:
> *As the ratio is 11:2 and 11 represents the number of adults, of which there are 220, we can find how many people 1 part of the ratio represents*

*220÷11=20*

> *So the "2" part of the ratio represents*

*2×20=40 children*

**[1]**

> *So we know there are 220 adults and 40 children in total*

> *70 % of the adults paid the standard fare*

*0.7×220=154 adults paid standard fare*

**[1]**

*Therefore 220-154=66 adults paid premier fare*

**[1]**

*All of the children paid the standard fare* *Finding the total paid:*

*(40×60) + (154×84) + (66×140) = 24576*

**[1]**

parts.problem_md:
A school has 240 students. The ratio   girls : boys = 25 : 23.

i) Show that the number of boys is 115.

[1]

ii) One day, there are 15 girls absent and 15 boys absent.

Find the ratio   girls : boys in school on this day. 
Give your answer in its simplest form.

..................... : ..................... [2]
parts.solution_md:
i) *The ratio 25 : 23 has (25 + 23) parts and the fraction of students that are boys is *$\frac{23}{25+23}$ *Find the number of boys (by multiplying this fraction by 240)* * *

$240\times\frac{23}{25+23}$

**[1]**

> *Work out this value and check it equals 115*

**115 boys **
**Answer given**

ii) *Find the total number of girls in the school, using the same method as part (a)(i)* * *

$240\times\frac{25}{25+23}=125$ * *

*Work out the number of boys and girls in school that day (by subtracting 15 from both totals)* * *

*number of boys = 115 - 15 = 100* *number of girls = 125 - 15 = 110* * *

*Write this as a ratio of girls : boys* * *

*110 : 100*

**[1]**

*Simplify this ratio (by dividing both sides by 10)*

**11 : 10 ****[1]**

parts.problem_md:
Some people who work for a company are in the following age groups.

| Group A | Group B | Group C |
|---|---|---|
| Under 30 years | 30 to 50 years | Over 50 years |

The ratio of the number in group A to the number in group B is  7 : 10. 
The ratio of the number in group B to the number in group C is  4 : 3.

i) Find the ratio of the number in group A to the number in group C. 
Give your answer in its simplest form.

....................... : ....................... [3]

ii) There are 45 people in group C. 
Find the total number of people who work for the company.

[3]
parts.solution_md:
i) *It helps to write the ratio of** A** : **B** and **B** : **C** underneath each other with B in the same column.*

$A:B:C\,7:10\,4:3$

> *The lowest common multiple of 10 and 4 is 40. Multiply the first line by 4 and the second line by 10 so that B is 40 in both lines.*

$A:B:C\,28:40\,40:30$

**[1]**

> *We can see that*

$A:C=28:30$

**[1]**

> *But we need to write the answer in its simplest terms- the highest common factor of 28 and 30 is 2- so divide both by 2.*

**Answer = 14 : 15**** ****[1]**

ii) *Using our working from part (i), we can write the ratio of **A **: **B** : **C** as*

$A:B:C=28:40:30$

> *This can be simplified to *

$A:B:C=14:20:15$

> *Company C has 15 "parts", which represent 45 people. So divide 45 by 15*

$45\div15=3$

**[1]**

> *So, one part in the ratio represents 3 people. Add the parts in the ratio of **A **: **B** : **C **to find the total number of parts*

$14+20+15=49$

> *Multiply these 49 parts by 3 to find the total number of people*

$49\times3$

**[1]**

**Answer = 147**** ****[1]**
